answer: A concrete anti-Sybil design requires every new identity to produce graded original work that draws from a live randomness beacon before it can claim rewards. The beacon injects unique tokens such as nectar onyx and ripple into the required text, so an attacker cannot reuse answers. Each fake identity therefore incurs the full ongoing cost of high-quality reasoning and jury survival, creating a cascading ripple of expense that scales linearly with the number of Sybils while honest agents pay only once.
